_note: Sixth use of the declared-input pattern, beside chooserLinkText, gameIdOverrides, copy-authorisation, support-pill and studioBand. Ruled by Matt 2026-08-13 in the AGX-1 reconciliation: the occupant check stops matching display titles and compares STABLE IDS - folder slugs - via this record, so a shelf title and a homepage box label are free to differ ('Rally Vector 3D' on the box, 'NEW - Rally Vector 3D - Championship Edition' on the shelf) without the gate calling honest copy a phantom. The mapping cannot be derived: the box label is authored homepage copy, the slug is the serving path, and nothing on the page binds them machine-readably. An occupant with no entry here fails the gate loudly - adding a box means adding a line here, which is the visible decision this record exists to force. This is not the return of the RULED_OCCUPANTS pin that the gate's own tenth-instance note warns about: that pin listed WHO may occupy (membership, which the shelf now decides), this record declares WHAT EACH LABEL MEANS (identity, which nothing else declares). WIDENED 2026-08-13 by Matt's ruling: a NEW· marker holder is the same class of fact as an occupant mapping - a declared shelf fact with exactly one writer - so it lives here rather than in a second mechanism. newReleaseHolder carries the slug of the game holding the ephemeral NEW· marker on the canonical shelf (MattRoper1977/Games games.json, the file the arcade fetches at runtime). This record is the single source for BOTH the occupant map and the marker holder: no verifier may hold a frozen copy of either, ever again. It replaced exactly two frozen copies - RULED_OCCUPANTS in tools/verify_surfaces.js and the inline '/olympics/' in tools/verify_olympics_live.mjs - each of which went stale silently because its workflow could not fire on main. The holder moved by site commits 69c1d57 and 3e6deb0 (the 2026-08-12 driving-games launch, Neon Meridian then Rally Vector 3D) and landed on the canonical shelf in Games aa3e3bf, which transferred the marker off Nova Siege in the same commit. Reading this record is not the same as trusting it: verify_olympics_live.mjs also reconciles it against the SERVED shelf, so a record that disagrees with production is a red.
_holderCaughtUp20260814: newReleaseHolder moved rallyvector3d -> emberwild. PRODUCTION MOVED FIRST and this record followed, which is the only direction it may ever travel: the canonical shelf decides who wears NEW·, and Games ca9a8c6 ('Emberwild takes the shelf, and the NEW marker with it', PR #32) transferred the marker to /emberwild/ on 14 August. This field was born stale rather than left to rot - ca9a8c6 landed BEFORE newReleaseHolder existed on main, so the very first value it carried was already behind the shelf. The disagreement was found the way it was meant to be, by marker-matches-record reporting 'served holder "/emberwild/" vs declared "/rallyvector3d/"'. THE OCCUPANT MAP IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: /main/ renders exactly three New Release boxes - Rally Vector 3D, Neon Meridian, Relicforge: Fracture Engine - and none of them is Emberwild, so there is no label to map. The two facts are not the same fact. occupants describes the homepage boxes; newReleaseHolder describes the shelf marker. A game can hold the marker without holding a box, and adding a row here for a box that does not exist would be this record leading production instead of following it.
_holderMoved20260827: The Titan Forge + Crown & Badge launch transfers NEW· atomically from /emberwild/ to /crownbadge/. The homepage occupant map remains unchanged: it describes three authored homepage boxes, while newReleaseHolder describes the one shelf marker.
